title: Yigit Koray Babal
text: Computational biologist with a decade of experience (since graduate research in 2016) turning large-scale, multimodal, high-dimensional biological data into statistically validated, actionable results, most recently across single-cell multi-omics, immune repertoire, and proteomics datasets in a neuroimmunology research field. Proficient in Python, R and SQL, with deep hands-on experience in distributed/HPC servers, containerized pipelines, and machine-learning-based analysis. Alongside the analysis work, I’ve independently built and administered the Linux server infrastructure behind it, from HPC/Slurm setup to multi-user services and clinical data governance.

title: Yigit Koray Babal
text:
Skills

Programming & data: Python, R, SQL, Git/GitHub, Bash
Statistics & machine learning: hypothesis testing and statistical modeling, ML-based clustering and classification, trajectory/pseudotime (time-series-style) inference, network inference algorithms, simulation and quantitative modeling
Multimodal data integration: combining heterogeneous, high-dimensional data streams (transcriptomic, epigenomic, proteomic, immune-receptor) into integrative analyses
Systems & infrastructure: 10 years as a Linux user; independently set up and administered a dedicated group server (full OS-admin rights): Slurm scheduling, conda/container environment management (Docker/Singularity), multi-user services (RStudio Server, Jupyter Notebook), and data storage/backup policy, including encryption and governance for clinical data
Reporting & tools: HTML/CSS, Shiny applications for interactive data reporting

title: Yigit Koray Babal
text:
Education

PhD in Biotechnology (2018-2023) | Gebze Technical University - Kocaeli, Turkey
MSc in Molecular Biology and Genetics (2016-2018) | Gebze Technical University - Kocaeli, Turkey
BSc in Biology (2012-2016) | Marmara University - Istanbul, Turkey

title: Yigit Koray Babal
text:
Research Experience

Postdoctoral Researcher (2025-Present) | University of Helsinki - Helsinki, Finland

Built statistical and machine-learning pipelines to profile immune cell populations from multimodal single-cell data, tracking how disease-modifying therapies shift cellular-level readouts over time in MS patients.
Own data management strategy for sensitive clinical research data (encryption, storage policy) and manage HPC project resources: user and data allocation, pipeline development, and containerization.

Postdoctoral Researcher (2023-2025) | Karolinska Institutet - Stockholm, Sweden

Modeled cell-cell interaction signals from multi-omic data to characterize brain-vascular changes in ALS and MS, integrating results across species for comparative analysis.
Set up and administered the group’s dedicated Linux server end-to-end (full OS-admin rights): configured Slurm job scheduling, deployed and maintained multi-user RStudio Server and Jupyter Notebook environments, and owned data storage and backup strategy.

Guest Researcher (2021-2022) | Max Planck Institute of Biological Intelligence - Munich, Germany

Ran trajectory and network-inference analyses on multimodal single-cell data (transcriptomic + epigenomic) to model neuron development, including motif enrichment and gene-oscillatory-network analysis.
Developed a Python tool implementing a lineage-tracing algorithm for single-cell DNA barcoding data.
Maintained Linux workstations and HPC cluster infrastructure for the group: built reproducible conda environments and Docker/Singularity containers for other researchers’ analysis workflows, with ongoing R/CLI tool maintenance.

Research Assistant (2019-2023) | Gebze Technical University - Kocaeli, Turkey

Performed transcriptomic and genomic analyses of nervous system development and gene regulation, including gene regulatory network inference.
Built quantitative kinetic models of transcription-factor regulation, and ran cell-culture-based validation experiments.
Maintained the department’s website (announcements, exam results) as governmental university staff, hand-coding HTML/CSS where the built-in CMS fell short.

title: Yigit Koray Babal
text:
Dvoretskova, E., Lynch, C., Bright, A.R., Babal, Y.K., Isaev, S., Kharchenko, P., Adameyko, I., & Mayer, C. (2026). bioRxiv (preprint). DOI: 10.64898/2026.05.25.727662
Using in vivo CRISPR perturbation, lineage barcoding, and single-cell transcriptomics in the developing mouse basal ganglia, we found that loss of the transcription factor Sp9 shifts progenitor fate from D2 toward D1 medium spiny neurons and intercalated cells. We further showed that SP9 activates genes directly at GC-rich promoters but represses them indirectly at distal enhancers by partnering with DLX factors and the NuRD corepressor complex — with the relative abundance of SP9 versus DLX determining which mode dominates, extending the combinatorial transcription-factor code to include factor stoichiometry.



Liao, K., Babal, Y.K., & Lewandowski, S.A. (2026). Annual Review of Animal Biosciences, 14, 297–317. DOI: 10.1146/annurev-animal-030424-071428
A review of the rare mammalian species capable of regenerating adult tissue with minimal scarring — such as antler regrowth in deer, skin regeneration in bats, and systemically reduced scarring in African spiny mice — summarizing the proposed cellular mechanisms behind these adaptations and their implications for future regenerative therapies.



Uyar, O.A., Babal, Y.K., Yilmaz, B., & Kurnaz, I.A. (2024). International Journal of Cell Biology, 2024, 6798897. DOI: 10.1155/2024/6798897
We showed that the transcription factor Elk-1 interacts with the mitotic kinases Aurora-A, Plk1, and Cdk1 through its N-terminal domain, mapped candidate phosphorylation sites, and confirmed kinase activity on Elk-1 peptides in vitro — proposing this interaction as a potential target for anticancer therapies.



Del-Valle-Anton, L., Amin, S., Cimino, D., Neuhaus, F., Dvoretskova, E., Fernandez, V., Babal, Y.K., Garcia-Frigola, C., Prieto-Colomina, A., Murcia-Ramon, R., et al. (2024). Science Advances, 10(13), eadn9998. DOI: 10.1126/sciadv.adn9998
Single-cell RNA sequencing combined with lineage barcoding of ferret cortical germinal zones revealed multiple radial glia progenitor classes that follow parallel differentiation trajectories converging on a common class of newborn neuron. This lineage multiplicity was conserved between ferret and human but absent in mouse, suggesting it underlies cortical expansion and folding in species with larger, gyrified brains.



Babal, Y.K., Sonmez, E., & Kurnaz, I.A. (2023). Biosystems, 227, 104891. DOI: 10.1016/j.biosystems.2023.104891
A comparative transcriptomics and gene regulatory network study across human, gorilla, mouse, fruit fly, and worm examining how ETS-family transcription factors regulate neuronal differentiation. The regulatory role of ETS proteins in nervous system development proved broadly conserved across species, with the ETS, PEA3, and ELF subfamilies most active in transcriptional regulation of neuronal differentiation.



Yurduseven, K., Babal, Y.K., Celik, E., Kerman, B.E., & Kurnaz, I.A. (2022). OMICS: A Journal of Integrative Biology, 26(5), 305–317. DOI: 10.1089/omi.2022.0023
We performed cell-type-specific interactome analysis of multiple sclerosis transcriptomic datasets, mapping protein interaction networks separately in white and gray matter and identifying hub proteins (including APP, EGLN3, PTEN, and LRRK2) that appear central to disease mechanisms. Comparing brain and peripheral blood expression further nominated biomarker candidates such as NRGN, CRTC1, CDC42, and IFITM3 for MS diagnostics.



Babal, Y.K., Kandemir, B., & Kurnaz, I.A. (2021). Journal of Personalized Medicine, 11(2), 138. DOI: 10.3390/jpm11020138
Analyzing microarray expression data from glioma patients across tumor grades, we identified ETS-family transcription factors (ETV1, ELK3, ETV4, ELF4, and ETV6) as candidate biomarkers for grade classification, and reconstructed their gene regulatory networks — comparing them against networks from ETS-overexpressing neuroblastoma cell lines to reveal both shared and tumor-specific regulatory relationships.
